summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style biography of Willie Cager, an African American basketball player on the 1966 Texas Western (now UTEP) team that won the 1966 national championship under coach Don Haskins. It covers his role in the championship game, his nickname and background, a heart murmur that limited his playing time, and his 1968 NBA draft selection by the Baltimore Bullets, which never led to a professional career.
one_line: Willie Cager was a player on the 1966 Texas Western national championship team who was drafted by the Baltimore Bullets but never played professionally.
key_facts: Willie Cager is described as an African American basketball player who was a member of the 1966 Texas Western (now UTEP) college basketball team.
Texas Western won the 1966 National Championship with Willie Cager on the roster.
Willie Cager was coached by the Hall of Fame coach Don Haskins at Texas Western.
Texas Western started an all-black starting lineup against the all-white University of Kentucky.
In Texas Western's championship game victory, Willie Cager scored eight points and grabbed six rebounds.
The school's website describes Willie Cager as "A skilled low post player" during his career.
Willie Cager was raised in New York City and was nicknamed "Scoops".
Willie Cager suffered from a heart murmur during the 1965–66 season.
Because of his heart murmur, Texas Western was forced to use Willie Cager sparingly, in four-minute shifts, until he recovered enough to play more.
After playing at Texas Western, Willie Cager was drafted by the Baltimore Bullets in the 12th round of the 1968 NBA draft.
Willie Cager never played as a professional, partly due to his health.
